subject: Partner telemetry & LangChain/LlamaIndex integration — Kuiper x Redwood
messages:
From: Aisha Gupta <aisha@kuiper.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Partner telemetry & LangChain/LlamaIndex integration — Kuiper x Redwood

Hi Marcus / Redwood team,

Thanks again for taking a call last week. Kuiper AI (we build TraceLayer, a lightweight tracing + prompt observability layer for LLM pipelines) would like to explore a pilot integration with Redwood Inference so we can capture end-to-end traces across the SDKs your ISV partners (LangChain, LlamaIndex) use. Our ask: a narrow pilot that wires TraceLayer into Redwood-hosted runtime so we can correlate request spans, KV cache events, and prompt/tool calls.

High-level items we want to validate in the pilot:
- Trace propagation hooks between Redwood runtime and LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters
- Minimal perf overhead (target <5% p95 token latency increase)
- Example telemetry schema (span names, tags, token counts) and export to Jaeger/OTLP

I've attached a short SOW and a compact integration checklist to this email. Can we schedule a 30-minute tech sync the week of Nov 15? Vanessa / Kimberly — looping you in for partnerships + procurement context.

Attachments: [Attachment: Kuiper_SOW_v1.pdf (application/pdf)]

Cheers,
Aisha Gupta
Head of Partnerships, Kuiper AI
aisha@kuiper.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha@kuiper.ai>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner telemetry & LangChain/LlamaIndex integration — Kuiper x Redwood

Thanks Aisha — appreciate the SOW and clear scope. Quick answers up front:
- We're interested in a pilot that focuses on LangChain and LlamaIndex SDK callsites and the hosted runtime trace boundary.
- Tech sync works for Nov 17 or Nov 18. 30 minutes is fine.

Pre-sync questions so we can prepare engineers:
1) Auth model for your tracing agent — do you require a push endpoint (OTLP) or would you prefer pull (we emit spans to an internal queue)?
2) Sample payloads — can you share a redacted example of the span payload and the expected span id correlation with requests?
3) Backwards-compatible behavior — if we need to add a small handshake header, is that sufficient for LangChain adapter instrumentation?

Vanessa / Kimberly — can you weigh in on procurement cadence and whether we need a PO / SOW approval before starting a technical POC? Mateo — looping you for any runtime constraints (GPU tracing overhead / kernel-level hooks).

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Partner Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Gupta <aisha@kuiper.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner telemetry & LangChain/LlamaIndex integration — Kuiper x Redwood

Hi Aisha — welcome, and thanks for the SOW. Quick product note from our side to make the pilot actionable:

Pilot proposal (30-day):
- Week 1: Tech sync + sample payload exchange. Agreement on trace contract (we prefer OTLP v1 with Jaeger-compatible span names).
- Week 2-3: LangChain adapter instrumentation (we'll provide a skeleton adapter and test harness). LlamaIndex indexer instrumentation for search/indexing ops.
- Week 4: Canary in staging + perf analysis and a short findings doc.

Tech asks / constraints:
- We already have a lightweight "trace v1" contract in the runtime — spans for request.start / request.end, token.generate span with token_count tag, and cache.hit / cache.miss events. If Kuiper can ingest that schema that's ideal (we'll share the schema).
- Any SDK-level instrumentation should be opt-in via a LangChain/LLI plugin flag so customers don't opt-in globally.
- Runtime: Mateo, please confirm whether adding OTLP span emission affects our KV cache behavior or if we should instrument at the adapter layer only.

Attachments: [Attachment: integration-checklist.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)], [Attachment: sample-telemetry-payload.json (application/json)]

Kimberly — procurement note: if the SOW is <= $25k, we can likely approve via existing partnership credits and a short contract; beyond that we'll need legal review and a PO.

Thanks — we can take Nov 17-19 for the sync. Marcus, please pick a slot and I'll invite the right engineers.

— Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Partnerships Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Gupta <aisha@kuiper.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Mateo Alvarez <mateo_alvarez@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Partner telemetry & LangChain/LlamaIndex integration — Kuiper x Redwood

Marcus / team — thanks for the quick back-and-forth. Confirming next steps:
1) Tech sync: Nov 18, 11:00 PT (Marcus / Mateo / Kuiper engs). We'll share a 20-min agenda: trace contract, auth model, test harness.
2) Kuiper will send a patched SOW v1.1 with an explicit POC milestone and a DocuSign link for a <= $20k engagement.
3) We'll upload sample payloads and a minimal LangChain adapter PR that demonstrates span creation (no production changes yet).

Links: HubSpot deal — https://app.hubspot.com/deal/10234-5678 (owner: A. Gupta), DocuSign (SOW v1.1) — https://www.docusign.com/sandbox/agree/ABCDEF123456

Kimberly — appreciate the procurement note. If you want, we can mark the initial POC as a pilot credit (no PO required) and then move to a paid SOW if the perf/regression criteria are met.

Looking forward to the sync.

Best,
Aisha
Head of Partnerships, Kuiper AI
